title: Automated ad rules
content:
# Automated ad rules

Pause, reactivate or rebudget campaigns, ad sets and ads automatically when their metrics cross a threshold, or get a webhook when they do.

An ad rule checks one ad account's campaigns, ad sets or ads on a schedule and acts on each that meets every condition.

It works on Meta, Google, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X and Reddit (dashboard: Ads > Rules).

## Start from a template

`GET /v1/ads/rules/templates` returns ready-made rules, each a full rule body.

Their `goal` groups them: `protect` (stop losers), `scale` (budget ladder, duplicate winners, shift budget to winners, Google target CPA room), `schedule` (night pause, morning restart, midnight reset) and `alert`.

1. Pick one and set `name`, `accountId` and `adAccountId`.
2. Adjust the thresholds to the account: amounts are in its currency.
3. Send it to `POST /v1/ads/rules` disabled, preview it, then enable it.

`platforms` lists the networks a template works on (null means all). In the dashboard, the create form offers the same templates.

## Create a rule

Call `POST /v1/ads/rules`. This one checks hourly and pauses every ad set with 7-day spend of at least 50 and cost per conversion above 25:

```bash
curl -X POST https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/rules \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Pause expensive ad sets",
    "accountId": "64f1c2e8a9b3d4e5f6a7b8c9",
    "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
    "level": "adset",
    "conditions": { "all": [
      { "metric": "cpa", "window": "last_7d", "op": ">", "value": 25 },
      { "metric": "spend", "window": "last_7d", "op": ">=", "value": 50 }
    ] },
    "actions": [{ "type": "pause" }, { "type": "notify" }],
    "schedule": { "everyMinutes": 60 },
    "enabled": false
  }'
```

Returns `201` with the rule. Create it disabled, preview it, then enable it.

| Field | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| `accountId` | The ads connection from `GET /v1/accounts`: platform `metaads`, `googleads`, `tiktokads`, `linkedinads`, `pinterestads`, `xads` or `redditads`. Never a posting account. |
| `adAccountId` | The ad account inside it, from `GET /v1/ads/accounts?accountId=<accountId>`. Must have `selected: true` there. |
| `level` | `campaign`, `adset` or `ad`; each object is checked on its own. |
| `campaignIds` | Optional: only these campaigns or their ad sets. Omit for the whole ad account. |
| `filters` | Optional: narrow by name or goal (`{ "field": "name", "op": "contains", "value": "Prospecting" }`), by id (`{ "field": "campaign_id", "op": "not_in", "values": ["123"] }`) by age (`{ "field": "days_live", "op": ">=", "value": 3 }`) by budget level (`{ "field": "budget_level", "op": "equals", "value": "campaign" }`), by Google campaign type ([below](#google-search-impression-share)) or by a recent change ([below](#skip-campaigns-that-just-changed)). Every filter must hold. |
| `conditions` | `all` (every condition holds) or `any` (one is enough), 1 to 10 conditions. |
| `actions` | What to do with each matching object. |
| `schedule.everyMinutes` | Run interval: 15, 30, 60, 180, 360, 720 or 1440. Defaults to 60. |
| `schedule.times` | Instead of an interval, set times each week in the ad account timezone, like `[{ "days": ["mon", "fri"], "at": "09:00" }]`. |
| `schedule.startsAt`, `schedule.endsAt` | Optional: the rule only runs between these two times. |
| `schedule.quietHours` | Optional: no runs between `from` and `to` each day in the ad account timezone, like `{ "from": "22:00", "to": "06:00" }`. |
| `cooldownMinutes` | Rest period per object after an action. Defaults to 1440. |

A condition compares one metric over one window with a number:

```json
{ "metric": "cpa", "window": "last_7d", "op": ">", "value": 25 }
```

- **Metrics**: `spend`, `impressions`, `clicks`, `conversions`, `ctr`, `cpc`, `cpm`, `cpa`, `roas`, `reach`, `frequency`. `ctr` is a percentage. Money is in the ad account currency.
- **Budget**: `daily_budget` is the daily budget. `budget_used` is spend as a percent of it per day of the window, so `today` `>=` 200 means twice the budget spent. Campaigns and ad sets only.
- **Reach and frequency** use the platform's de-duplicated reach, so they work on Meta and TikTok only. Elsewhere, summed daily reach would overstate both. On Google campaign rules, `frequency` reads Google's own figure ([below](#google-search-impression-share)).
- **Your own results**: `result:<key>` reads a metric you send or a formula over it, such as `result:cac_percent`, on campaign rules only. A campaign with no value for it never matches. See [Send your results per campaign](/guides/campaign-results).
- **Windows**: `today`, `yesterday`, `last_3d`, `last_7d`, `last_14d`, `last_30d`, `this_month`, `last_month`. Days follow the ad account's timezone; `last_7d` is the 7 full days before today, and only `today` and `this_month` read the day in progress. `this_month` runs from the 1st through today, and `last_month` is the whole previous month.
- **Custom windows**: `<from>_to_<to>_days_ago`, such as `8_to_2_days_ago`, reads full days in that range. Use it to skip recent days whose conversions are still arriving. At most 90 days back.
- **Calendar**: `day_of_month` and `working_day_of_month` read today's date in the ad account's timezone. Use them to wait until a month's numbers mean something, such as `working_day_of_month` `>=` 5 (Monday to Friday, holidays not counted). They take `window: "today"` and no `compareTo`.

This pauses a campaign once its spend this month passes 10,000, from the fifth working day on:

```json
{ "all": [
  { "metric": "spend", "window": "this_month", "op": ">", "value": 10000 },
  { "metric": "working_day_of_month", "window": "today", "op": ">=", "value": 5 }
] }
```

Send alerts through your own Slack and mailbox by listing them on `notify`:

```json
{ "type": "notify", "send": [{ "accountId": "<slack account>", "channelId": "C0123" }, { "accountId": "<gmail account>", "to": "ops@acme.com" }] }
```

Use `op: "top"` or `"bottom"` to act on the best or worst objects instead of a fixed threshold. This matches the 3 ad sets with the highest CPA over the last 7 days:

```json
{ "metric": "cpa", "window": "last_7d", "op": "top", "value": 3 }
```

Add `compareTo` to compare a metric with its own past. `value` is then a ratio: this fires when yesterday's CPC is at least twice its average over the 28 days before:

```json
{ "metric": "cpc", "window": "yesterday", "op": ">=", "value": 2, "compareTo": "30_to_2_days_ago" }
```

`compareTo: "previous_period"` uses the same number of days just before the window. For `this_month` it is the same days of last month, and for `last_month` the month before. Counts like spend are compared per day.

`compareTo: "usual"` compares with the median of the same days on the 4 previous weeks, for windows of up to 7 full days: `yesterday` against the same weekday.

`"of": "usual"` reads that usual value itself, to judge only campaigns big enough to matter:

```json
{ "all": [
  { "metric": "conversions", "window": "yesterday", "op": "<=", "value": 0 },
  { "metric": "conversions", "window": "yesterday", "of": "usual", "op": ">=", "value": 2 }
] }
```

`compareTo: "usual_deviation"` is how many median absolute deviations of the same 4 weeks the window sits from their median.

The deviation counts as at least 5% of the median, so weeks that barely vary (spend held by its budget) do not turn a 1% move into dozens of deviations.

Pair it with a ratio to ignore a campaign's normal swings:

```json
{ "all": [
  { "metric": "spend", "window": "today_so_far", "op": ">=", "value": 1.6, "compareTo": "usual" },
  { "metric": "spend", "window": "today_so_far", "op": ">=", "value": 3, "compareTo": "usual_deviation" }
] }
```

It never matches when those weeks all read 0. Hourly windows also take `budget_used`, spend as a percent of today's daily budget: `today_so_far` `>=` 80 is 80% of the budget spent already.

Hourly windows read data only on ad accounts the hourly sync covers, and read as unknown elsewhere. `GET /v1/ads/rules/hourly-windows` says which case an ad account is in.

Combine conditions with `all` and `any`, and nest groups up to 3 levels and 10 conditions in total.

This pauses an ad set whose CPC is above 2, or that spent 50 today with no conversion:

```json
{
  "any": [
    { "metric": "cpc", "window": "today", "op": ">", "value": 2 },
    { "all": [
      { "metric": "spend", "window": "today", "op": ">=", "value": 50 },
      { "metric": "conversions", "window": "today", "op": "<", "value": 1 }
    ] }
  ]
}
```

The dashboard edits one `all` or `any` list. A rule with nested groups shows them there and is changed through the API.

| Action | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `notify` | Sends the [`ad_rule.triggered`](/webhooks/ads/ad-rule-triggered) webhook with the matched objects. Subscribe an endpoint with `POST /v1/webhooks/settings` first, or a notify-only rule shows only its run history. |
| `notify` with `send` | Also sends a short alert to a Slack channel or an email address, through a Slack account or a Gmail, Outlook or IMAP mailbox you connected. Up to 5. |
| `pause` | Pauses the campaign, ad set or ad. |
| `activate` | Reactivates what a rule paused, once the cooldown has passed. With `includeManuallyPaused: true`, also what you paused. |
| `adjust_budget` | Changes the daily budget. `direction`: `increase` or `decrease`. `percent`: up to 100 up, 90 down. `limit`: increases never go above it, decreases never below. Not on ad-level rules. |
| `adjust_budget` with `amount` | Sets the daily budget to exactly `amount`, such as a reset every midnight. Not with `direction`, `percent` and `limit`. |
| `duplicate` | Copies the campaign or ad set with its ads, paused unless `status` is `active`. Meta and TikTok campaigns and ad sets, LinkedIn campaigns. |
| `adjust_bid` | Moves a Meta ad set's bid cap or cost cap, by a step (`direction`, `percent`, `limit`) or to an exact `amount`. Ad sets without a cap are skipped. |
| `adjust_target` | Moves a Google campaign's `target`: `cpa` (target CPA, in the ad account currency) or `roas` (target ROAS, a ratio: 3 is 300%), by a step or to an exact `amount`, inside the bid strategy the campaign is on. Portfolio strategies and strategies without that target are skipped. |
| `reallocate_budget` | Moves daily budget from the matched objects ranked worst to those ranked best. See [Move budget to what works](#move-budget-to-what-works). |
| `edit_name` | Tags the name: `add` puts text like `[WINNER]` at the start (or the end with `at: "end"`), `remove` takes it out. Meta, TikTok and Reddit campaigns, ad sets and ads, and Google, LinkedIn and Pinterest campaigns and ad sets. Pair with a `name` filter so a second rule acts on tagged objects. |

`pause`, `activate` and `adjust_budget` take an optional `maxChangesPerDay` (1 to 100): the rule then changes at most that many objects in any 24 hours, across runs.

Every action that changes ads also takes an optional `maxChangesPerObject` (1 to 100): the rule changes one object at most that many times, counted over 400 days.

Matches over the limit are skipped with `daily_limit_reached` and tried again later.

## Google Search impression share

A Google campaign rule can read the share of Search impressions a campaign won, and the share it lost to budget or ad rank, in percent over the window:

```json
{ "metric": "search_budget_lost_impression_share", "window": "last_7d", "op": ">=", "value": 20 }
```

- **Metrics**: `search_impression_share`, `search_budget_lost_impression_share`, `search_rank_lost_impression_share`. A share lost to budget means the campaign runs out of budget before the day ends; a share lost to rank means its bids or ad quality lose auctions.
- **`frequency`** on Google is the average number of times a person saw the campaign's ads over the window, as Google reports it for Display, Video and Demand Gen campaigns.
- They are read live from Google, campaign rules only. They do not go in groups, budget moves or `usual`, and a backtest does not replay them.
- A campaign Google gives no value for (impression share on a Display campaign) never matches.

Pick campaign types with the `channel_type` filter, Google rules only:

```json
{ "field": "channel_type", "op": "in", "values": ["DISPLAY", "VIDEO", "DEMAND_GEN"] }
```

Types: `SEARCH`, `DISPLAY`, `SHOPPING`, `HOTEL`, `VIDEO`, `MULTI_CHANNEL`, `LOCAL`, `SMART`, `PERFORMANCE_MAX`, `LOCAL_SERVICES`, `TRAVEL`, `DEMAND_GEN`.

## Skip campaigns that just changed

A new budget or bid strategy moves a campaign's numbers for a few days. The `days_since_change` filter reads the platform's change history, so a rule can wait those days out:

```json
{ "field": "days_since_change", "change": "budget", "op": ">=", "value": 3 }
```

- **`change`**: `budget`, `bidding`, `status` or `goal`. On Meta, an edit of one of the campaign's ad sets counts for the campaign.
- **`op`**: `>=` keeps campaigns left alone that long; `<` picks the ones changed within that many days. A campaign with no change in the history passes `>=`, unless a very busy account's history was cut short before that many days.
- **`value`**: 1 to 28 days.

It works on campaign rules on Meta and Google. Google records an edit of conversion goals as a campaign update naming no field, so `goal` reads those.

On Google, a change to a shared (portfolio) bid strategy is not read as a `bidding` change of its campaigns: only edits on the campaign itself count.

A backtest has no change history, so a rule with this filter matches nothing there.

## Move budget to what works

`reallocate_budget` ranks the objects the rule matched by `metric` over `window`, takes budget from the worst `from.count` and gives it to the best `to.count`. The total daily budget stays the same.

```json
{
  "type": "reallocate_budget",
  "metric": "roas",
  "window": "last_7d",
  "from": { "count": 2 },
  "to": { "count": 2 },
  "percent": 20,
  "maxChangesPerDay": 4
}
```

- **How much.** `percent` of each giver's budget, or `amount` in all, taken evenly. Receivers share it evenly.
- **Best end.** Lower is better for `cpa`, `cpc`, `cpm`, `frequency` and cost-type results (cost per sale, %CAC), higher otherwise. Set `best` to `highest` or `lowest` to change it. An object that spent with no result on a lower-is-better metric ranks worst and only gives.
- **Bounds.** A giver keeps at least `minBudget` and a tenth of its budget. A receiver stays at or under `maxBudget`; what receivers cannot take stays with the givers.
- **Who takes part.** Only objects that hold a daily budget at the rule's level: on Meta, campaign rules move CBO budgets and ad set rules move ad set budgets. Google shared budgets are left out. With fewer ranked objects than `from` plus `to`, givers take at most half.
- **All or nothing.** When `maxChangesPerDay` would hold back any change, none is made. Receivers are raised only after every giver's cut applied; otherwise they fail and the move is tried again on the next run.
- **Amounts.** Moved in the currency's smallest unit: whole yen or won. A move counts as raising spend for the free ads allowance.
- **Limits.** Not with `lifecycle` or `groups`. Undo puts back one object's budget at a time.

## Judge campaigns as groups

A campaign rule judges each campaign on its own numbers. To decide per product, channel or the whole account instead, add `groups`.

Each group is a name and filters. A group with no filters holds every campaign the rule checks.

```json
"groups": [
  { "name": "MBA", "filters": [{ "field": "name", "op": "contains", "value": "MBA" }] },
  { "name": "Account total", "filters": [] }
]
```

Each group's spend, conversions and your [results](/guides/campaign-results) are added up across its campaigns, and rates and formulas are computed on the totals.

If the MBA campaigns are at 10%, 75% and 100% %CAC, the MBA is at its total spend over its total revenue, not 75%.

The conditions are judged once per group, and a matching group acts on each of its campaigns, each keeping its own cooldown and daily cap.

- Paused campaigns count toward a group's totals; only the ones the rule may act on change.
- A campaign in several groups is acted on once per run, by the first matching group.
- A campaign with no results sent for the window counts as none: its spend is in the group's total and its revenue is 0. Send a row for every campaign, even with zeros, before a group rule reads your results.
- A rate you send as is (a percent or ratio with no formula) cannot be added up, so it reads as unknown for a group: define it as a formula over counts instead.
- Up to 20 groups. Reach, frequency and impression shares cannot be added up across campaigns, so they are not available with groups.
- The preview lists each group's totals under `groups`, and each campaign with the `group` it was judged in.

With `this_month`, an account-wide spend ceiling is one rule: notify when the `Account total` group's spend this month passes your forecast.

## Alerts instead of every run

Add `lifecycle` to act and notify once per episode. An object acts only after matching `confirmChecks` runs in a row, 1 to 5.

```json
"lifecycle": { "confirmChecks": 2, "hold": { "all": [{ "metric": "cpa", "window": "today", "op": ">", "value": 35 }] } }
```

The alert stays open while the conditions or `hold` match, and is critical while `critical` matches. It goes back to warning, without a notification, when `critical` stops matching.

The `escalated` webhook is sent once per alert. The alert resolves when both clear, after a pause or reactivation, a day after the object stops delivering (`not_evaluated`), or when the rule changes.

`GET /v1/ads/rules/{ruleId}/alerts` lists them, and `automation.alert.*` [webhooks](/webhooks/ads#ad-rules) announce each change.

Sending `lifecycle: null` removes it and closes the rule's open alerts.

## Preview before you enable

`POST /v1/ads/rules/{ruleId}/preview` runs the conditions on current metrics without acting. It returns, per object, whether it matches and each condition's actual value, plus the windows' timezone.

## Enable the rule

Send `PATCH /v1/ads/rules/{ruleId}` with `enabled: true`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/rules/RULE_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "enabled": true }'
```

## Read the run history

`GET /v1/ads/rules/{ruleId}/runs` lists runs from the last 31 days, newest first, each with an `outcome`:

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| `triggered` | Objects matched and the rule acted; `actedObjectIds` lists them. |
| `no_match` | No object met every condition. |
| `cooldown` | Objects matched, but all were in cooldown. |
| `failed` | Metrics unreadable, every action failed, or a notify-only rule's webhook could not be sent. `error` says why. |

- **`evaluation.notification.status`**: `done` once the webhook is queued for your subscribed endpoints. With none subscribed it is still `done`, but nothing is delivered.
- **Not queued**: `notification` is `failed` with a `reason`; a notify-only rule's run is `failed` too.

## Undo a change

`POST /v1/ads/rules/activity/{activityId}/undo` puts back a pause, reactivation, budget, bid or target change, or name tag, using an `id` from `GET /v1/ads/rules/activity`. The undo shows in the activity feed as a change of its own.

It is refused with `409` when the change was already undone, is a copy, or the object changed since, for example a budget someone edited afterwards.

## Write the rule as an automation

[`/v1/automations`](/guides/automations) serves the same rules in the shape every Zernio automation shares: a `trigger`, the `subjects`, the `conditions`, the `steps` and the `limits`.

An automation created there is also an ad rule with the same id, and the reverse. This is the rule above:

```bash
curl -X POST https://zernio.com/api/v1/automations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Pause expensive ad sets",
    "trigger": { "type": "schedule", "every": "1h" },
    "subjects": { "each": "adset", "adAccounts": [{ "accountId": "64f1c2e8a9b3d4e5f6a7b8c9", "adAccountId": "act_1234567890" }] },
    "conditions": { "all": [
      { "metric": "cpa", "window": "last_7d", "op": ">", "value": 25 },
      { "metric": "spend", "window": "last_7d", "op": ">=", "value": 50 }
    ] },
    "steps": [{ "type": "ads.pause" }, { "type": "notify.send" }],
    "limits": { "cooldown": "1d" }
  }'
```

It starts paused. `POST /v1/automations/preview` shows what it would match before you save it, and `POST /v1/automations/{automationId}/activate` turns it on.

When something does not fit, the 400 lists each problem with its path in `details.problems`. To edit, send the fields you change to `PATCH /v1/automations/{automationId}` with the `version` you read as `If-Match`.

## How it behaves

- **Combining actions.** A rule takes `notify`, plus at most one of `pause`, `activate`, `adjust_budget`, `adjust_bid`, `adjust_target`, `reallocate_budget`, `duplicate` and `edit_name`. Those need `cooldownMinutes` at least as long as the schedule.
- **Set times** follow the ad account timezone, daylight saving included. Without a known timezone they read as UTC.
- **End date.** After `endsAt` the rule stays enabled but no longer runs.
- **Metric lag.** Metrics are synced from the ad platform and can trail its own reporting.
- **Empty rates.** A rate with no denominator never matches: a `cpa` condition skips objects with no conversions.
- **Your own pauses.** `activate` leaves them alone unless the action sets `includeManuallyPaused: true`. But if you reactivate then pause an object between two runs, Zernio cannot tell your pause from the rule's and may reactivate it.
- **Google budgets.** Ad groups have no budget, so `adjust_budget` needs a campaign-level rule.
- **Batch size.** A run changes at most 20 objects; the rest wait for the next run. `maxChangesPerDay` caps it further.
- **Failed actions** get no cooldown, so the next run retries them.
- **No ads access** pauses all rules until access returns.
- **Allowance.** Past the free live-ads allowance without a payment method, reactivations and budget increases are skipped (`ads_allowance_exceeded`).
- **Disabling** stops runs until you re-enable.

## If it fails

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| `403` `ads_addon_required` | The team has no ads access. | Enable ads on the plan. |
| `403` `ad_account_not_selected` | The ad account is not selected on the connection. | Add it in the dashboard picker, or via `GET /v1/connect/{platform}/ads` with `adAccountIds` (the full list: it replaces the selection). |
| `400` `invalid_field_value` on `cooldownMinutes` | Cooldown shorter than the schedule on a rule that changes objects. | Raise `cooldownMinutes` to at least `schedule.everyMinutes`, or the shortest gap between two `schedule.times`. |
| `400` `invalid_field_value` on `actions` | `adjust_budget` on an ad-level rule, or on a Google ad set rule. | Use `level: "campaign"` (or `adset` outside Google). |
| `400` `invalid_field_value` on `conditions` | `reach` or `frequency` on a network other than Meta or TikTok (Google takes `frequency` on campaign rules), an impression share off a Google campaign rule, or a `result:` metric on an ad set or ad rule. | Use another metric on that network, or `level: "campaign"` for results and Google metrics. |
| `403` `ads_allowance_exceeded` | Reactivating or budget-raising rule, team past its free live-ads allowance without a payment method. | Add a payment method. Pausing and lowering rules still work. |
| `404` `resource_not_found` | No such rule, or another team's. | Check the `ruleId`. |
